 Live Reporting
 Charlotte Coates
 Most recent Most popular Remembrance Day published at 12:28 GMT 12:28 GMT 
 Chelsea v Manchester United (12:30 GMT) 
 Simon Stone 
BBC Sport Manchester United reporter at Stamford Bridge 
 This is the closest Chelsea home Premier League fixture to Remembrance Day.
 Representatives of the armed services are on the pitch for the annual minutes' silence and playing of the Last Post.
 0 0 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Lacroix is in attendance to support Chelsea published at 12:27 GMT 12:27 GMT 
 Chelsea v Manchester United (12:30 GMT) 
 Nizaar Kinsella 
BBC Sport Chelsea reporter 
 Maxence Lacroix is at Stamford Bridge today, but in his usual street clothes as he continues his recovery from a hamstring injury.
 As first reported by BBC Sport yesterday, the France international, 26, could be out until 2027 as concerns grow over the severity of the injury he sustained at Liverpool on Wednesday night.
 It is a blow for manager Xabi Alonso, who has started the £52m signing from Crystal Palace in all but one match in all competitions this season.

 'Got to start shining a light on the players' published at 12:26 GMT 12:26 GMT 
 Chelsea v Manchester United (12:30 GMT) 
 Glenn Murray 
Former Brighton striker on Premier League Kick-Off 
 It is a tough one because I personally believe that Michael Carrick loves that football club and I don't think they will get anyone as selfless as him. 
 You have got to start shining a light on the players. They have seen off manager after manager. 
 I know it's very difficult to manage a club the size of Manchester United, but I feel as though you have got to start looking at other places other than the manager.

 Post published at 12:25 GMT 12:25 GMT 
 Chelsea v Manchester United (12:30 GMT) 
 Right then, we've made it. 
 The teams are making their way onto the pitch as I type this.

 'Incompetence' published at 12:24 GMT 12:24 GMT 
 Chelsea v Manchester United (12:30 GMT) 
 Nigel Reo-Coker 
Former Aston Villa midfielder on Premier League Kick-Off 
 When you look at Manchester United you have got to say how dysfunctional of a football club they are.
 The fans cheered Michael Carrick off and they booed the players. 
 It shows that the two people (Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox) under Sir Jim Ratcliffe have no idea what they're doing, and they're showing complete incompetence in the position they are in. 
 86 8 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Everybody needs to improve' published at 12:23 GMT 12:23 GMT 
 Chelsea v Manchester United (12:30 GMT) 
 Mark Schwarzer 
Former Chelsea and Fulham goalkeeper on BBC Radio 5 Live 
 Image source, Reuters Michael Carrick is the leader and the players need to follow suit. 
 Everybody needs to improve and they need to show unity.
 57 18 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Steve Holland watching the warm-up published at 12:21 GMT 12:21 GMT 
 Chelsea v Manchester United (12:30 GMT) 
 Simon Stone 
BBC Sport Manchester United reporter at Stamford Bridge 
 Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick has not come out for the warm-ups, but his assistant Steve Holland is looking across the pitch from the touchline.
 Holland is back on familiar territory, having worked at Chelsea for eight years across a variety of roles before departing in 2017 to work with Gareth Southgate and the England team.
 The 56-year-old was viewed as an astute appointment to Carrick's backroom team last season when United surged into third place and secured a return to the Champions League after a two-year absence.
 Now, questions are being asked of Holland, given United's inability to control games.
 32 24 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 get involved Get Involved published at 12:19 GMT 12:19 GMT 
 Use 'Get involved' to have your say 
 Can Utd sack Carrick and keep Wilcox in his role? Almost certainly not. Interesting conundrum for Berrada. 12 managers in 13 years, pretty clear that the manager isn't the real problem.
 Ben, Oxford 
 By end of the day United will be in a relegation scrap, and I don't see that changing through out November. It's bad when you consider the match against Coventry in December a potential 6 pointer.
 Christopher, Blackburn 
 I think most people expect Chelsea to continue their relatively positive start to the season (apart from the Spurs game). It will be tough for United to pick up even a point here today.
 George, Birmingham 
 101 23 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Cole is a smart guy' published at 12:17 GMT 12:17 GMT 
 Chelsea v Manchester United (12:30 GMT) 
 Cole Palmer saw red quite literally in the defeat to Tottenham last weekend but today he's back in the Chelsea team and will be looking to make amends. 
 Here's what Xabi Alonso has had to say about his number 10: "We have spoken about the game and things we can improve. 
 "But, we always do. We don't want it repeated but for him it is the first one. So we have talked more about football because Cole is a smart guy."
 Image source, Getty Images 
 17 45 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Improvement across the board is necessary' published at 12:15 GMT 12:15 GMT 
 Chelsea v Manchester United (12:30 GMT) 
 The Manchester United boss will be in charge at Stamford Bridge on Saturday despite a run of eight games without a win in all competitions. Captain Bruno Fernandes could also feature after "clear-the-air talks" with his head coach.
 Fernandes was dropped for the home defeat to Bournemouth after criticising Carrick's tactics in the Champions League loss at Como, but the Portugal international's influence and ability will probably be needed if United are to alter their downward trajectory.
 The Red Devils have won only 29% of their 17 Premier League games without Fernandes starting since he joined from Sporting Lisbon in 2020, in comparison to winning 49% of 233 when he does start.
 Even if the manager-captain row has been resolved to the point of Fernandes returning to the team, wholesale improvement across the board is also necessary with United facing the prospect of failing to win nine matches in a row for the first time since 1988.

 Chelsea v Manchester United (12:30 GMT) 
 Dion Dublin 
Former Man Utd and Aston Villa striker on BBC Radio 5 Live 
 Image source, Reuters On Man Utd warm- up... 
 There is not enough effort. They deserve to get started on - they have not been playing well. There is enough talent there to not play that way. It is about the players having a bit of pride.

 get involved Get Involved published at 12:10 GMT 12:10 GMT 
 Click 'Get Involved' on this page to have your say 
 You’d think with all the talk about the players letting Carrick down and putting his job in jeopardy, they would have got their heads together and decided they’re going to at least look like they could be bothered.
 Andy, Cardiff 
 147 16 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Tough talking this week at Man Utd published at 12:08 GMT 12:08 GMT 
 Chelsea v Manchester United (12:30 GMT) 
 Simon Stone 
BBC Sport Manchester United reporter at Stamford Bridge 
 Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick says ‘hard
conversations’ are needed sometimes for any team to reach its optimum level.
 United seem to have been in chaos since Lisandro Martinez
spoke out against the club’s recruitment strategy following the 2-0 defeat by
Atletico Madrid earlier this month.
 The 4-1 defeat to Como, followed by a 3-0 home loss to
Bournemouth have left Carrick hanging to his job by a thread.
 The United boss held clear-the-air talks with skipper Bruno
Fernandes on Wednesday, and he must hope his side deliver a winning performance
at Stamford Bridge which would end their eight-match run without a win.
 Carrick tried to portray a ‘business as usual’ stance in his
news conference on Thursday but he accepts life cannot always be easy.
 “It's pretty clear,” he said. “It's not always rosy and nice
conversations between anyone, whether that's between me and the players,
between me, (director of football) Jason (Wilcox) or (chief executive) Omar
(Berrada) or the owners. 
 “It's the truth, it's the hard truth at times and it's what
we need to move forward.”
 28 25 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Alonso needs a win published at 12:06 GMT 12:06 GMT 
 Chelsea v Manchester United (12:30 GMT) 
 Xabi Alonso isn't exactly having the best of times at Chelsea at the moment and could really do with three points today. 
 The Blues were knocked out of the Carabao Cup by Liverpool on Wednesday and were beaten on home turf by rivals Tottenham last Saturday. 
 Image source, Getty Images 
 42 18 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Bruno, Bruno' published at 12:04 GMT 12:04 GMT 
 Chelsea v Manchester United (12:30 GMT) 
 Simon Stone 
BBC Sport Manchester United reporter at Stamford Bridge 
 There are not many Manchester United fans in the away section at Stamford Bridge just now but there was an audible 'Bruno, Bruno' from them when Bruno Fernandes led the outfield players out for their warm-up.
 I suspect there will be a unified effort to get management, players and fans moving in the same direction at least for the start of today's game at Stamford Bridge.
 Manchester United are staring at the possibility of a nine-game winless streak in all competitions for the first time since 1988-89.
 Image source, Getty Images

 Chelsea v Manchester United (12:30 GMT) 
 Image source, Reuters Manchester United could end today in the Premier League bottom three, if results go against them. 
 That'd be a proper Halloween scare for the United fans.

 Manchester United are winless in their last eight games in all competitions (D3 L5). They last had a longer run in October/November 1988 with nine.

 Disappointing that Mainoo did not make it. Midfield will need a big step-up. Would have preferred Cunha instead of Mount. If we see 100% effort and the right attitude, it's possible. 100% support for Carrick no matter what.
 Alan, Spain

 Man Utd's last four Premier League results published at 11:54 GMT 11:54 GMT 
 Chelsea v Manchester United (12:30 GMT) 
 Manchester United's last four Premier League results don't make for pretty reading at all. Just the three points. 
 Throw in a 4-1 loss away at Como in the Champions League, too. 
 48 24 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Expect tough, and intense game' published at 11:52 GMT 11:52 GMT 
 Chelsea v Manchester United (12:30 GMT) 
 Chelsea 
 Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso, speaking to TNT Sports: "We are back in Premier League mode, so it is the most important. 
 "For sure, today is a big one. We need a good game and a good performance."
 On Estevao starting: "Because he is ready, because he has been preparing and training well. Today he is needed, and we hope he enjoys his game and that he can have a good impact."
 On whether Morgan Rogers will be the main centre forward: "Too early to tell, so we will see. It could, but we have options."
 On Jordan Henderson's exclusion : "He is ill, no injury, but he was not feeling well yesterday, and today he had a fever."
 On Man Utd : "We expect a tough game, and intense game against United. They are a big team and good players, so we will need our best."
